_note: Named areas larger than a country, each one an explicit list of ISO3 codes. A group with scope 'continental' shades every country in its area. This is the only honest way to draw one: the countries are real, their borders are already on the map, and nothing is invented. An earlier version drew a circle of arbitrary radius instead, which over Lebanon was mostly sea.
_membership_note: Membership follows the UN M49 geoscheme, a published standard rather than our own opinion. Where a country's inclusion is arguable, that is a conversation for the Pocket Project rather than a decision for this file.
_not_in_basemap_note: These belong to their region and are correct as data, but the 1:50m basemap does not draw them: they are microstates, small islands or, in Antarctica's case, outside the country layer. They will simply not shade. Listed so the consistency check can tell a deliberate omission from a typo.
_why_all_of_them: All seven continents are defined, not just the two we currently need. If only Africa and Latin America existed as continental areas, then a pan-European or pan-Asian group would have no way to be described the same way, and the map would show Europe resolved to cities while Africa was one block. That asymmetry would be a property of this file rather than of the network, and in collective trauma work that particular flattening is not a neutral accident.

latin_america.label: Latin America
latin_america.note: Crosses two continents, which is why it is a macro-region rather than a continent. The Spanish and Portuguese speaking countries of the Americas plus the French speaking Caribbean, per UN M49's Latin America and the Caribbean minus the anglophone states.

southern_africa.label: Southern Africa
southern_africa.note: Not currently used. The Southern Africa Practice Group records South Africa and is placed in Cape Town; if the Pocket Project would rather show it across the region, this is here.

balkans.label: The Balkans
balkans.note: Defined because an Integration Lab is devoted to it and the Lab's own text calls the region a mosaic of nations. Unused until the Pocket Project says so.

_label_at_note: Where to print the region's name on the map. Derived from the basemap, not chosen freely: for most regions it is the area-weighted mean of the member countries' centroids, verified to fall inside a member country. Europe, North America and Oceania are set by hand, because area weighting put them in Siberia, central Canada and Papua New Guinea respectively, which is inside the region but not where anyone looks for the name. The label states which shaded area is which; the shading itself still carries the extent, and nothing here asserts a boundary.
